newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Euro stocks rise as US rates stay unchanged.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Euro stocks rise as US rates stay unchanged.

text.p: European stock markets rose on Wednesday after the U.S. Federal Reserve decided against raising interest rates, though some investors believed it was only delaying the day when rates would inevitably rise.

On the foreign exchange markets, the dollar recovered a little from a fall triggered when the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), the policy arm of the U.S. central bank, announced on Tuesday that short term rates were unchanged.

Markets had been divided before the FOMC announced its decision on whether the Fed Funds rate would rise by 0.25 percentage points as a pre-emptive strike against inflation, or not. The decision came after European markets had closed.

Some investors believed that, by delaying a move, the Fed would have to raise rates more when the FOMC next meets in early July. But this view was not universally shared due to the dominant role of Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan.

"People are saying Greenspan should have raised rates by the expected quarter point and that now he will have to raise them by half a point in July," said one London dealer. "But that's so much hot air. He's the man calling the shots."

The London market got a helping hand from Wall Street, where the Dow Jones Industrial Average had been down 70 points at Tuesday's European close. It later got a boost from the FOMC news and closed up 74.58 points or 1.03 percent at 7,303.46.
The FTSE 100 index of blue chips was up 28.8 points or 0.63 percent to 4,636.3 by mid morning on Wednesday.
Dealers expect the London market to consolidate as some investors believe the Fed should have moved now to avoid a bigger rate rise later. Domestic issues are also weighing on sentiment.
A decision by new Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown to reform financial services regulation reinforced worries about his forthcoming first budget, they said.
"He's proved that he is a man in a fair hurry," said one dealer. "People will now be looking for the tax reforms that they were worrying about before the election."
A possible rise in British interest rates, which would be the second since Labour won the May 1 election, was also likely to cap gains.
The Paris market was also firmer following the Fed decision with the CAC 40 index up 32.55 points or 1.18 percent at 2,783.66. But business was thin. "There's no volume," lamented one broker.

The German market likewise rose on the Fed news. The DAX index was up 34.41 points or 0.97 percent at 3,577.84 despite an overnight tumble for the dollar, which lost nearly three pfennigs against the mark. A stronger mark adds to the problems German exporters are facing.
The dollar crept higher in Europe, extending a mild recovery from the overnight drop which followed the announcement of no change in U.S. interest rates.
It also suffered overnight after a senior Bank of Japan official was quoted as saying that the central bank was considering the timing of a decision on raising Japanese interest rates.
Later the BOJ, which is now concerned by the rapid rise of the yen, said the official had been misquoted. Trying to soothe markets, it said there were no immediate plans for a rate rise.
The dollar was at 114.02 yen at midmorning compared with 113.80 at the European close on Tuesday. It fell below 113 in late U.S. trading on Tuesday.

"The FOMC decision and BOJ comments haven't had a lasting impact. We're seeing signs of fresh investor buying this morning," said a U.S. bank dealer in London. "We expect a few days of consolidation but people seem to be bargain-hunting here."

The market focus was on U.S. March trade data due at 1230 GMT on Wednesday. An average of analysts' forecasts pointed to a $10.3 billion deficit, little changed from February's $10.4 billion shortfall.
The dollar was at 1.6889 marks, after closing in Europe on Tuesday at 1.6953 and hitting a low later of just above 1.67.
On precious metals, palladium was fixed at $180.50 an ounce, the highest level since April 1989 and up $0.75 from Tuesday afternoon.
STOCK PRICES AT 0900 GMT
London's FTSE 100 was was up 28.8 points or 0.63 percent to 4,636.3.
The Paris CAC-40 index was up 32.55 points or 1.18 percent at 2,783.66.
Frankfurt's DAX index was up 34.41 points or 0.97 percent at 3,577.84
CURRENCIES
The dollar stood at 1.6889 marks and 114.02 yen compared with 1.6953 marks and 113.80 yen in late European trade on Tuesday.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended at $342.75 ounce, unchanged from Tuesday's close in London. Silver was down two cents at $4.69.
